context:
Treat runtime benchmark identity as a registry contract, not a string
formatting convenience. First pin current mismatches with tests, then replace
the heuristic and adjust validation to fail early for unknown IDs. Keep
output path tests nuanced: canonical identity must match the registry, while
data-source output locations may deliberately refer to the source benchmark.
description:
Independent verification at checked SHA e60986923 confirmed the critic's
highest-risk finding directionally, with one important correction: the public
`benchbox.base.BaseBenchmark._get_benchmark_name()` heuristic mismatches 8
registry IDs, not 9. `tpcds_obt` does not use `_get_benchmark_name()` because
it still inherits the deprecated core base; it has a related name heuristic
risk through `benchbox.core.base_benchmark.BaseBenchmark.name`, but its
constructor explicitly writes to `benchmark_runs/datagen/tpcds_obt_sf1`.

Confirmed mismatches for public-base core classes:
  read_primitives -> readprimitives
  write_primitives -> writeprimitives
  metadata_primitives -> metadataprimitives
  ai_primitives -> aiprimitives
  transaction_primitives -> transactionprimitives
  joinorder_synthetic -> joinordersynthetic
  tpch_skew -> tpchskew
  vector_search -> vectorsearch

Runtime leakage was confirmed through logger names for all 8 mismatches, and
through default output paths for direct callers of classes such as
`TPCHSkewBenchmark` and `VectorSearchBenchmark`. Some data-sharing benchmarks
intentionally override their output directory to the canonical TPC-H datagen
path after base initialization, so output-path impact is not uniform. The
runner path is likely shielded when it passes explicit `benchmark_name` and
output directories, but this still needs end-to-end confirmation before code
changes.

Independent verification also confirmed `validate_scale_factor("unknown_bench",
999)` returns silently in `benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py` before the
loader eventually fails elsewhere. This is actionably related: benchmark ID
validity and canonical identity should fail early and consistently.

anti_patterns.why: that keeps the heuristic alive and recreates registry drift.

anti_patterns.dont: infer canonical IDs by lowercasing class names
anti_patterns.why: underscores and acronym boundaries are part of the registry contract.

anti_patterns.dont: launch long-running benchmark runs to verify identity
anti_patterns.why: targeted instantiation, dry-run, and contract tests are sufficient.

anti_patterns.dont: treat source-data output directories as identity
anti_patterns.why: primitives may reuse TPC-H data while still being separate benchmarks.

preserves.behavior: Data-sharing benchmarks that intentionally reuse TPC-H datagen paths keep that output behavior unless a separate product decision changes it.
No live/cloud benchmark execution is required for this fix.
Scale-factor validation for known benchmarks keeps existing error types for unsupported scales.
The registry remains the single source of truth for benchmark IDs; do not add an untested parallel dict.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py: BENCHMARK_CLASS_NAMES and CORE_BENCHMARK_CLASS_NAMES - reuse as the class-to-ID source of truth.
benchbox/utils/path_utils.py: get_benchmark_runs_datagen_path - preserve intentional data-source output directory conventions.
tests/unit/core/test_benchmark_api_contract.py: public contract invariants - reuse for unknown-ID and canonical-ID contract coverage.
tests/unit/core/test_loader_registry_parity.py: registry/loader parity checks - extend to runtime identity parity.

work_units.notes:

loader class, instantiates with `get_benchmark_default_scale()`, and
records `(registry_id, class, runtime_id, output_dir, logger_name)` for
any mismatch. Commit only a compact markdown or TODO note if durable
evidence is needed; keep raw stdout in `/tmp`.

work_units.notes:
Prefer a registry-derived reverse map from
`CORE_BENCHMARK_CLASS_NAMES`/`BENCHMARK_CLASS_NAMES` before adding a new
class attribute. If a class attribute is chosen, add a registry parity
test that fails when it diverges. Account for wrappers, core classes,
subclasses such as `TPCHSkewBenchmark`, and data-sharing benchmarks whose
output directory intentionally points at the source benchmark.
work_units.summary: Design the canonical benchmark-id source for runtime instances

work_units.notes:
Change `benchbox/base.py` so runtime identity, logger names, validation
fallbacks, and default direct-call output paths use the canonical registry
ID. Do not hard-code another special-case mapping inside the base class.
Preserve intentional data-source output overrides for primitives that
reuse TPC-H data.
work_units.summary: Replace `_get_benchmark_name()` heuristic with registry-backed canonical resolution

work_units.notes:
Extend the existing parity/contract tests so every loader benchmark that
exposes runtime identity is checked against its registry ID. Include
explicit assertions for `tpch_skew`, `vector_search`,
`joinorder_synthetic`, and the primitives. Separate assertions for
intentional data-source output directories from assertions for canonical
benchmark identity.
work_units.summary: Add all-benchmark parity tests for runtime identity, logger names, and direct default paths

work_units.notes:
Update `validate_scale_factor()` or its caller contract so an unknown
benchmark ID raises a clear `ValueError`/`KeyError` before class loading.
Add tests for unknown ID, invalid scale for a known ID, and valid default
scale for all registered benchmarks. Preserve existing
`ScaleFactorNotSupportedError` behavior for unsupported known scales.
work_units.summary: Make scale validation reject unknown benchmark IDs at the earliest registry boundary

If a lightweight dry-run is sufficient, use it; do not launch live/cloud
workloads.
